chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding the contracted slave (mukatab), when he pays part of his contract, he said: 'The people used not to stipulate conditions, and today they do stipulate, and the Muslims are bound by their conditions. So if it was stipulated upon him that if he was unable (to pay), he would be returned (to slavery), then he is returned; and if it was not stipulated upon him, he is not returned.'
And regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Contract them if you know in them any good.' He said: 'Contract them if you know that they have wealth.'

He said, 'And he said regarding the contracted slave: His master stipulates upon him that he should not marry except with his permission until he pays off his contract.' He said: 'It is befitting for him not to marry except with permission from him, for it is a condition for him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the legal conditions for a contracted slave (mukatab) regarding payment, reversion to slavery, and marriage in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'al-Muslimun 'ala shurutihim' (Muslims are bound by their conditions) within the context of mukatabah, affirming that contractual stipulations regarding reversion to slavery or marriage restrictions are legally binding. It connects the legal framework to the Quranic verse 24:33, interpreting 'knowing good in them' as financial capability, thereby grounding the juristic ruling in divine revelation.
